discovery: Discovery of the double pulsar PSR J0737-3039A/B and its use for the most precise strong-field tests of general relativity

nominees.name: Michael Kramer
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy, Bonn, Germany

nominees.name: Marta Burgay
nominees.affiliation: INAF - Osservatorio Astronomico di Cagliari, Italy

nominees.name: Andrew G. Lyne
nominees.affiliation: Jodrell Bank Centre for Astrophysics, University of Manchester, UK

motivation: In 2003 Burgay and colleagues found a 22.7-ms pulsar in a 2.4-hour orbit at Parkes, and Lyne and colleagues then detected radio pulses from its companion. PSR J0737-3039A/B is the only known system in which both neutron stars are seen as pulsars. It is a unique laboratory for gravity. Led by Kramer, 16 years of timing across the world's large radio telescopes measured seven post-Keplerian parameters. They confirmed the gravitational-wave damping predicted by general relativity to better than 0.02%, detected relativistic spin precession, and resolved effects of higher order than the quadrupole formula, including light-propagation effects and the loss of mass-energy through rotation. These are the most precise strong-field tests of Einstein's theory in the radiative regime. They complement the binary-pulsar work honoured in 1993 and LIGO's direct detections, and show how precision pulsar timing turned a chance discovery into fundamental physics.
